cases.d: Verify the Secretary can plan the agenda in Draft, WaitingApproval, Rejected, Approved, Published and InProgress.
steps: For a meeting in each of the six statuses, as its Secretary send POST /api/meetings/<id>/agenda with body { "title": " Báo cáo ", "presenterId": "<id of the Member>", "documentIds": ["<id of a meeting document>"] }.
Send GET /api/meetings/<id>/agenda.
exp: Each create returns HTTP 201 Created with code "MSG60" ("Tạo mục nghị sự thành công.") and Location /api/meetings/<id>/agenda.
The agenda lists one item titled "Báo cáo" (trimmed) with the presenter and the linked document.
pre: One meeting per status, each with a Secretary, a Member and one uploaded document.

cases.d: Verify the agenda requires sign-in, hides itself from outsiders and reports the caller's role.
steps: GET /api/meetings/<id>/agenda without authentication.
As an outsider, GET the agenda of this meeting and of a random meeting id.
As the Secretary, GET the agenda.
exp: Anonymous: HTTP 401 Unauthorized.
Outsider: HTTP 404 for both, with identical bodies.
Secretary: HTTP 200 OK with an empty items list and permissions for the Secretary role.
pre: A meeting with no agenda item, a Secretary and an unrelated outsider.

cases.d: Verify an invalid agenda body returns MSG66 and writes nothing.
steps: As the Secretary, POST /api/meetings/<id>/agenda with each body: presenterId "bad"; "Title" in the wrong case; title twice; an extra status; actualStartedAt; presenterName; {}; null; [].
exp: Each request returns HTTP 400 Bad Request with code "MSG66" ("Thông tin mục nghị sự không hợp lệ.") and errors.
No agenda item is created.
pre: A Draft meeting with its Secretary signed in and no agenda item.

cases.d: Verify malformed Unicode in a property name returns a validation error without changes.
steps: As the Secretary, send create, update and reorder requests whose JSON property name is the lone surrogate \ud800, then \udc00.
exp: Each request returns HTTP 400 with code "MSG66" (or "MSG143" for reorder).
The agenda and the realtime event count are unchanged.
pre: A meeting with agenda items and its Secretary signed in.

cases.d: Verify field limits, duplicate ids, presenter and document checks.
steps: As the Secretary, create items with: a 301-character title; a 4001-character description; an empty guest presenter id; both a guest and a member presenter; an outsider as presenter; the empty UUID as presenter; the same document twice; the empty UUID as document; a document of another meeting.
exp: Each request returns HTTP 400 with code "MSG66" naming the field (title, description, presenter or documentIds).
No item is created.
pre: Two meetings with documents; the Secretary of the first is signed in.

cases.d: Verify update, delete and reorder keep fixed positions and document links.
steps: Link the document to item 2 (PUT), then link it to item 1 (PUT).
DELETE item 2.
Reorder the remaining items with PUT /agenda/order.
exp: Updates return HTTP 200 with code "MSG61"; the document moves to item 1.
Delete returns HTTP 200 with code "MSG62"; the document stays linked to item 1.
Reorder returns HTTP 200 with code "MSG63".
pre: A Draft meeting with three agenda items and one document.

cases.d: Verify starting and completing items follows role, state and the server clock.
steps: As the Secretary, POST /agenda/<item 1>/current and /agenda/<item 1>/complete.
As the Chair, start item 1, then try to start item 2.
As the Chair, complete item 1.
exp: Secretary: HTTP 403 with code "MSG73" for start and "MSG74" for complete.
Chair start: HTTP 200 with code "MSG64"; second start: HTTP 409 with code "MSG72" ("Đã có mục nghị sự đang diễn ra.").
Complete: HTTP 200 with code "MSG65"; actual start and end times are set by the server.
pre: An InProgress meeting with a Chair, a Secretary and Pending items.

cases.d: Verify an Ended meeting's agenda is read-only and a meeting not running cannot execute items.
steps: On the Ended meeting, as the Secretary POST a new item and GET /agenda/editor-options.
As the Chair, start and complete an item.
Repeat start on a Published meeting that has not started.
exp: Planning returns HTTP 409 with code "MSG67".
Start returns HTTP 409 with code "MSG73"; complete returns HTTP 409 with code "MSG74".
pre: An Ended meeting and a Published meeting with agenda items.

cases.d: Verify each failed save rolls back and sends no realtime event.
steps: Stop PostgreSQL just before each request: create (Secretary), update, delete, reorder, start (Chair), complete (Chair).
exp: Create returns HTTP 503 with code "MSG68", update "MSG69", delete "MSG70", reorder "MSG71", start "MSG75", complete "MSG76".
Message: "Không lưu được thao tác nghị sự. Vui lòng thử lại.".
After restart the agenda is unchanged and no other viewer received an update.
pre: An InProgress meeting with agenda items; Chair and Secretary signed in.

cases.d: Verify a read failure returns MSG128 and a realtime push failure does not undo a saved change.
steps: Stop PostgreSQL and GET the agenda.
Restart PostgreSQL, stop the realtime hub delivery and create an item.
exp: The read returns HTTP 500 with code "MSG128" ("Không tải được chương trình nghị sự.").
The create returns HTTP 201 with code "MSG60" and the item is saved.
pre: A meeting with three agenda items and its Secretary signed in.

cases.d: Verify a system administrator, a presenter or another meeting's Secretary gain no agenda role.
steps: Give the Member the system Admin role and make them presenter of item 1.
As the Member, create an item and start item 1.
As the Secretary of another meeting, create an item here.
exp: Create returns HTTP 403 with code "MSG67"; start returns HTTP 403 with code "MSG73".
The other meeting's Secretary is refused.
pre: An InProgress meeting with agenda items and a second meeting with its own Secretary.

cases.d: Verify reorder can move Done and current items and a no-op keeps the update time.
steps: Reorder four items so the Done item and the current item move.
Send the same order again.
exp: The first reorder returns HTTP 200 with code "MSG63".
The repeat changes nothing; updatedAt stays the same.
pre: A meeting with four items: item 1 Done, item 3 InProgress.

cases.d: Verify unlinking a document does not delete it, and an inactive presenter must be replaced.
steps: Set item 1 presenter to the Member with the document, then save it without the document.
Start and complete item 1 as the Chair.
Deactivate the Member and update item 1 keeping the Member as presenter.
exp: Both updates return HTTP 200 with code "MSG61"; the document still exists in the meeting documents.
Start and complete succeed (MSG64, MSG65).
Keeping an inactive presenter is refused with code "MSG66".
pre: An InProgress meeting with a Chair, a Secretary, a Member and a document.

cases.d: Verify a delete blocked by a database constraint keeps notes and the agenda.
steps: Add a meeting note attached to item 1 and another note for the meeting.
As the Secretary, DELETE /agenda/<item 1>.
exp: HTTP 503 with code "MSG70".
Both notes and the agenda item remain.
pre: A meeting with agenda items on PostgreSQL.

cases.d: Verify completing with an invalid actual time fails without changing the evidence.
steps: Mark item 1 InProgress without an actual start time (test data).
As the Chair, POST /agenda/<item 1>/complete.
exp: HTTP 503 with code "MSG76".
The item stays InProgress with no actual end time.
pre: An InProgress meeting on PostgreSQL.

cases.d: Verify a failure linking several documents rolls back the new item.
steps: Add a database trigger that fails when the document "Injected link failure" is linked.
As the Secretary, create an item linking a normal document and that document.
exp: HTTP 503 with code "MSG68".
No new item and no document link is saved.
pre: A meeting with two documents on PostgreSQL.

cases.d: Verify ending a meeting rolls back the agenda change and the history when the save fails.
steps: As the Chair, start item 1.
End the meeting while the database fails on save.
exp: The end is refused.
Item 1 stays InProgress and no end history row is written.
pre: An InProgress meeting on PostgreSQL.

cases.d: Verify a cancelled request is cancelled, not reported as a business error.
steps: Pause PostgreSQL, send GET /agenda and POST /agenda, and cancel both in the client before they answer.
exp: The requests are cancelled; the backend log shows cancellation, not a failure code.
pre: A meeting with agenda items and its Secretary signed in.

cases.d: Verify a slow realtime publish after commit does not lose or misreport the saved item.
steps: Slow down the realtime hub so publishing takes longer than the request timeout.
As the Secretary, create the item "Committed".
Repeat with the publish failing after the timeout.
exp: The item "Committed" is saved in both runs.
The response reports success; the late failure is only logged.
pre: A meeting with no agenda item on PostgreSQL.

cases.d: Verify the agenda demo data only inserts and survives user edits and deleted items.
steps: Start the backend on a development database with the demo accounts.
Rename the running demo meeting to "User edit" and delete its fourth agenda item.
Restart the backend.
exp: After restart the title is still "User edit" and the deleted item is not recreated.
pre: Development database with thuky, chutoa and thanhvien.

cases.d: Verify simultaneous creates get distinct positions.
steps: As the Secretary, send 8 POST /agenda requests at the same time (Postman runner, parallel).
exp: All 8 return HTTP 201.
The agenda has 11 items with 11 distinct positions 1 to 11.
pre: A meeting with three agenda items.

cases.d: Verify two simultaneous starts have one winner and one current item.
steps: As the Chair, send two start requests at the same time, for the same item and then for two different items.
exp: One request returns HTTP 200 and the other HTTP 409.
Exactly one item is InProgress.
pre: An InProgress meeting with Pending items.

cases.d: Verify two reorders from the same snapshot do not silently overwrite each other.
steps: GET the agenda and keep orderVersion.
Send two PUT /agenda/order at once with that orderVersion and different orders.
exp: One returns HTTP 200 with code "MSG63".
The other returns HTTP 409 with code "MSG143" ("Chương trình nghị sự đã thay đổi. Vui lòng tải lại.").
pre: A meeting with three agenda items and its Secretary signed in.

cases.d: Verify an update waiting for the meeting lock rechecks state and role.
steps: In psql, lock the meeting row (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) and keep the transaction open.
As the Secretary, send PUT /agenda/<item 1> with title "Updated after lock".
Inside the open transaction, in turn: start the item, end the meeting, change the Secretary's role, remove the Secretary; then commit.
exp: Item started: the update succeeds (HTTP 200, "MSG61").
Meeting ended: HTTP 409 with code "MSG67".
Role changed: HTTP 403 with code "MSG67".
Secretary removed: HTTP 404.
pre: An InProgress meeting on PostgreSQL.

cases.d: Verify a reorder waiting behind a change to the item set detects the stale snapshot.
steps: GET the agenda; lock the meeting row in psql.
Send PUT /agenda/order with the snapshot's orderVersion.
Inside the lock, start an item / delete an item / create an item, then commit.
exp: The reorder returns HTTP 409 with code "MSG143" in each case.
pre: A meeting with three agenda items on PostgreSQL.

cases.d: Verify ending the meeting saves the agenda only together with the meeting end.
steps: As the Chair, start item 1.
End the meeting, then roll the end back (database failure).
exp: Item 1 is closed only when the meeting end is saved; after the rollback it is still InProgress.
pre: An InProgress meeting on PostgreSQL.

cases.d: Verify a guest sees the agenda with document names but no write permission and no user identities.
steps: As the Secretary, link a document to item 1.
As an invited guest with a verified session, GET the agenda.
exp: HTTP 200 OK.
Every permission is false.
Items show document metadata but no internal user ids or emails.
pre: A Published meeting with a verified guest invitation.

cases.d: Verify a guest cannot use editor options or any change, even with a colliding user id.
steps: As the guest, GET /agenda/editor-options, PUT /agenda/<item>/conclusion, POST /agenda, PUT /agenda/order, POST /agenda/<item>/current.
Repeat with a guest token whose subject equals the Secretary's id.
exp: Every request returns HTTP 403 Forbidden.
The agenda and events are unchanged.
pre: A Published meeting with a verified guest invitation.

cases.d: Verify the guest's access is checked again on every read.
steps: As the guest, GET the agenda.
Revoke the invitation, expire the session, mark it unverified or remove the session; GET the agenda again after each.
exp: The first read returns HTTP 200.
After each change the read returns HTTP 404.
pre: A Published meeting with a verified guest invitation.

cases.d: Verify a guest sees the agenda only when a member could.
steps: As an invited guest, GET the agenda of a Draft, WaitingApproval, Rejected, Approved, Published and Ended meeting.
exp: Draft, WaitingApproval, Rejected and Approved return HTTP 404.
Published and Ended return HTTP 200.
pre: One meeting per status, each with a guest invitation.

cases.d: Verify guest access is denied when the guest access adapter is not configured.
steps: Run the backend with the default (unavailable) guest access adapter.
GET the agenda with a guest token.
exp: HTTP 404 Not Found.
pre: A Published meeting with a guest invitation.

cases.d: Verify an invalid identity, an expired token or an adapter failure never returns data.
steps: GET the agenda with a guest token for an empty invitation id.
Make the guest store fail and GET the agenda.
GET the agenda with an expired guest token.
exp: Invalid identity: HTTP 404.
Store failure: HTTP 500 with code "MSG128".
Expired token: HTTP 401.
pre: A Published meeting with a guest invitation.

cases.d: Verify guest realtime updates are scoped to the meeting and the session and recipients are rechecked.
steps: Open three guest sessions in separate browsers: two for this meeting (different sessions), one for another meeting; join each meeting's hub.
As the Secretary, change the agenda of this meeting.
Revoke one guest session and change the agenda again.
exp: Both guests of this meeting receive agendaChanged; the other meeting's guest receives nothing.
After revocation only the remaining session receives the next change.
pre: Two Published meetings with guest invitations.

cases.d: Verify realtime agenda changes reach only joined, authorized readers.
steps: Open the meeting in browsers for the Secretary, the Member, an outsider and a member of another meeting; each joins this meeting's hub.
As the Secretary create an item, update it, reorder; as the Chair start and complete it.
exp: The Secretary and the Member see each change live.
The outsider and the other meeting's member receive nothing.
pre: Two InProgress meetings on PostgreSQL.

cases.d: Verify a viewer who loses access stops receiving updates.
steps: The Member joins the hub and sees an agenda change.
Deactivate the Member / remove them / soft-remove them / mark them delegated.
As the Secretary, change the agenda again.
exp: The first change arrives.
After the access change no further event arrives.
pre: A Published meeting with a Member.

cases.d: Verify a no-op or failed write sends nothing and leaving is per connection.
steps: The Member joins the hub in two tabs.
As the Secretary, save an item without changes, then make a failing write.
Leave the meeting in the first tab and make a real change.
exp: No event for the no-op or the failed write.
After leaving, the second tab still receives the real change.
pre: A Published meeting with a Member.

cases.d: Verify a token in the query string works only for the hub and an expiring connection closes.
steps: GET /api/meetings/<id>/agenda?access_token=<member token> without an Authorization header.
POST /hubs/meetings/negotiate?negotiateVersion=1&access_token=<member token>.
Connect to the hub with a token about to expire and wait past expiry.
exp: The API request returns HTTP 401.
The negotiate request returns HTTP 200.
The hub connection is closed when the token expires.
pre: A Published meeting with a Member.

cases.d: Verify loading the agenda uses the same number of queries for 1 item or 50 items with documents.
steps: Enable SQL logging.
GET the agenda of a meeting with 1 item, then of a meeting with 50 items, 4 documents each and a guest presenter.
exp: Both reads return HTTP 200.
The number of SQL queries is the same for both.
pre: Two meetings on PostgreSQL as described.

cases.d: Measure 100 active users reading the agenda and resynchronising in real time (not a deployment certification).
steps: Create 100 users on the roster of a meeting with 50 items.
Have each user read the agenda and join the hub (load script).
Make one agenda change and measure when every client has resynchronised.
exp: Every read succeeds.
All 100 clients receive the change; timings are recorded for information only.
pre: A local PostgreSQL test database and a load script.

cases.d: Verify removing a participant clears them as presenter of every item at once or rolls back.
steps: Make the Member (or a guest) presenter of several items.
Remove the Member (or revoke the guest), once normally and once with a database failure.
exp: On success, every item loses that presenter in one change.
On failure, the participant and all presenters are unchanged.
pre: A Published meeting with agenda items on PostgreSQL.

cases.d: Verify a conclusion waiting for the meeting lock rechecks the minutes and the role.
steps: Lock the meeting row in psql.
As the Secretary, PUT /agenda/<done item>/conclusion.
Inside the lock: create minutes / change the Secretary's role / remove the Secretary; commit.
exp: With minutes: HTTP 409 with code "MSG273".
Role changed: HTTP 403 with code "MSG273".
Removed: HTTP 404.
pre: An InProgress meeting with a Done item on PostgreSQL.

cases.d: Verify assigning a presenter waiting for the lock rechecks removal or revocation.
steps: Lock the meeting row in psql.
As the Secretary, set the guest (or Member) as presenter of item 1.
Inside the lock, revoke the guest (or remove the Member); commit.
exp: The assignment is refused with code "MSG66"; item 1 keeps its presenter.
pre: A Published meeting with a guest and a Member on PostgreSQL.

cases.d: Verify two simultaneous conclusions store one whole content, author and time.
steps: As the Chair and the Secretary at the same time, PUT the conclusion "Chair" and "Secretary" for the same Done item.
exp: Both requests succeed.
The stored conclusion is exactly one of the two, with that person as author and a matching time.
pre: An InProgress meeting with a Done item.

cases.d: Verify the agenda migration keeps old data, adds constraints and refuses a lossy downgrade.
steps: Create a database at the migration before SynchronizeAgendaWithPoRequirements and insert legacy agenda data.
Upgrade to the latest migration.
Try to downgrade back.
exp: After upgrade the legacy data is kept and the new constraints exist.
The downgrade stops with an error instead of losing data.
pre: A local PostgreSQL test database.

cases.d: Verify presenter and shared documents can be changed for Pending, InProgress and Done items.
steps: For item 1 in each status, as the Secretary, set a guest presenter and link a document; then switch to a member presenter.
exp: Each update returns HTTP 200 with code "MSG61".
pre: A meeting with a guest invitation and documents.

cases.d: Verify the server decides when a conclusion can be written.
steps: As the Chair and the Secretary, GET the agenda and PUT a conclusion for: InProgress meeting / InProgress item; InProgress / Done; Ended / Done; InProgress / Pending; Published / Done; and any meeting that already has minutes.
exp: The first three return HTTP 200 with code "MSG271" ("Lưu kết luận mục nghị sự thành công.").
The others return HTTP 409 with code "MSG273".
canEditConclusion in the agenda matches each result.
pre: Meetings and items in those states.

cases.d: Verify the conclusion body rejects invalid or forged fields.
steps: As the Chair, PUT /agenda/<item>/conclusion with each body: {}; conclusion null; "  "; 3; "Conclusion"; conclusion twice; an extra conclusionUpdatedById; an extra title.
exp: Each request returns HTTP 400 with code "MSG272".
No conclusion is saved.
pre: An InProgress meeting with a started item.

cases.d: Verify conclusion length, failure, permission and not-found answers.
steps: As the Chair, save conclusions "A", 2000 characters and 1000 emoji, each with spaces around.
Save 2001 characters.
Send a non-JSON body, then stop the database and save.
As the Member, save a conclusion; as the Chair, save for an unknown item.
exp: Valid lengths return HTTP 200 with code "MSG271" and are trimmed.
2001 characters: HTTP 400 with code "MSG272".
Non-JSON: HTTP 415; database down: HTTP 503.
Member: HTTP 403 with code "MSG273"; unknown item: HTTP 404.
pre: An InProgress meeting with a started item.

cases.d: Verify any Pending item can be started and an old presenter name is not an assignment.
steps: Set a legacy presenter name "Historical name" on item 3.
As the Chair, GET the agenda and start item 3.
exp: Every Pending item shows canSetCurrent true.
Item 3 starts (HTTP 200, "MSG64"); the legacy name does not notify anyone.
pre: An InProgress meeting with three Pending items.

cases.d: Verify presenter notifications use the right channel and only a presenter change notifies.
steps: For a Draft, Approved, Published and InProgress meeting: set the Member as presenter of item 1, then change only the title, then switch to a guest presenter.
exp: Every update returns HTTP 200 with code "MSG61".
In Draft and Approved no one is notified.
In Published and InProgress only the presenter changes notify the new presenter (the title change does not).
pre: One meeting per status with a Member and a guest invitation.

cases.d: Verify a Secretary who makes themselves presenter is not notified.

req.as: Authorization: Bearer <access token of the meeting Secretary>

exp: HTTP 200 OK with code "MSG61".
The Secretary is the presenter.
No presenter notification is created.
pre: A Published meeting with agenda items.

cases.d: Verify presenter notifications are not duplicated, recheck the recipient and a failure does not undo the change.
steps: Make the notifier fail, then assign the Member as presenter.
Send the same assignment notification twice.
Remove the Member, then trigger the notification.
exp: The assignment is saved even though the notification failed.
Only one notification is stored for the same assignment.
No notification goes to a removed member.
pre: A Published meeting with a Member on PostgreSQL.

cases.d: Verify an invalid guest presenter rolls back the information and the links.
steps: As the Secretary, update item 1 with title "Must roll back", a document and a guest presenter that belongs to another meeting, is revoked, or does not exist.
exp: Each request returns HTTP 400 with code "MSG66".
Item 1 keeps its old title, presenter and documents.
pre: Two meetings, one with a revoked guest invitation.

cases.d: Verify reorder needs at least two items and refuses the old body format.
steps: GET the agenda of a meeting with one item.
PUT /agenda/order with its orderVersion and the single id.
PUT /agenda/order with the old body format (a list of positions).
exp: permissions.canReorder is false.
Both requests return HTTP 400 with code "MSG143" ("Danh sách sắp xếp phải chứa đúng mỗi mục nghị sự một lần.").
pre: A meeting with exactly one agenda item.

cases.d: Verify minutes in any status lock the conclusion, even with empty content.
steps: Create empty minutes for the meeting.
For each minutes status, as the Secretary PUT the conclusion "Locked".
exp: Each request returns HTTP 409 with code "MSG273".
No conclusion is saved.
pre: An InProgress meeting with a started item.
